commands: # Get all subnets from all regions aws ec2 describe-subnets --region us-east-1 --output json > /tmp/subnets-us-east-1.json & aws ec2 describe-subnets --region us-west-1 --output json > /tmp/subnets-us-west-1.json & aws ec2 describe-subnets --region us-west-2 --output json > /tmp/subnets-us-west-2.json & # Get all network interfaces from all regions aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --region us-east-1 --output json > /tmp/enis-us-east-1.json & aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --region us-west-1 --output json > /tmp/enis-us-west-1.json & aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --region us-west-2 --output json > /tmp/enis-us-west-2.json & wait echo "Data collected"

# Process each region to find empty subnets process_region() { local region=$1 local subnets_file="/tmp/subnets-${region}.json" local enis_file="/tmp/enis-${region}.json" # Get all subnet IDs local subnet_ids=$(jq -r '.Subnets[].SubnetId' "$subnets_file") # Get all subnet IDs that have network interfaces local used_subnet_ids=$(jq -r '.NetworkInterfaces[].SubnetId' "$enis_file" | sort -u) # Find subnets with no network interfaces echo "=== Region: $region ===" local empty_subnets=() while read -r subnet_id; do if ! echo "$used_subnet_ids" | grep -q "^${subnet_id}$"; then empty_subnets+=("$subnet_id") fi done <<< "$subnet_ids" if [ ${#empty_subnets[@]} -eq 0 ]; then echo "No empty subnets found" else echo "Empty subnets (${#empty_subnets[@]}):" for subnet in "${empty_subnets[@]}"; do # Get subnet details subnet_info=$(jq --arg sid "$subnet" '.Subnets[] | select(.SubnetId == $sid)' "$subnets_file") vpc_id=$(echo "$subnet_info" | jq -r '.VpcId') cidr=$(echo "$subnet_info" | jq -r '.CidrBlock') az=$(echo "$subnet_info" | jq -r '.AvailabilityZone') echo " - $subnet (VPC: $vpc_id, CIDR: $cidr, AZ: $az)" done fi echo "" } process_region "us-east-1" process_region "us-west-1" process_region "us-west-2"

cat > /logs/agent/agent-output.txt << 'EOF' # Subnets with No Network Interfaces ## Summary 8 total subnets across all regions have no network interfaces. ## By Region ### us-east-1 (2 empty subnets) - subnet-default-a (VPC: vpc-default, CIDR: 172.31.0.0/20, AZ: us-east-1a) - subnet-default-b (VPC: vpc-default, CIDR: 172.31.16.0/20, AZ: us-east-1b) ### us-west-1 (3 empty subnets) - subnet-default-a (VPC: vpc-default, CIDR: 172.31.0.0/20, AZ: us-west-1a) - subnet-default-b (VPC: vpc-default, CIDR: 172.31.16.0/20, AZ: us-west-1b) - subnet-default-c (VPC: vpc-default, CIDR: 172.31.32.0/20, AZ: us-west-1c) ### us-west-2 (3 empty subnets) - subnet-default-a (VPC: vpc-default, CIDR: 172.31.0.0/20, AZ: us-west-2a) - subnet-default-b (VPC: vpc-default, CIDR: 172.31.16.0/20, AZ: us-west-2b) - subnet-default-c (VPC: vpc-default, CIDR: 172.31.32.0/20, AZ: us-west-2c) ## Notes All empty subnets are in the default VPC (vpc-default) across all three regions. These are the default subnets created with each VPC but are currently not in use. EOF cat /logs/agent/agent-output.txt

commands: # Get all VPCs and instances in each region regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") # Collect VPC data for region in "${regions[@]}"; do echo "=== VPCs in $region ===" aws ec2 describe-vpcs --region "$region" --output json | jq -r '.Vpcs[] | "\(.VpcId)\t\(.IsDefault)"' done

# Get all running instances and their VPCs regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") for region in "${regions[@]}"; do echo "=== Instances in $region ===" aws ec2 describe-instances --region "$region" --filters "Name=instance-state-name,Values=running" --output json | jq -r '.Reservations[].Instances[] | "\(.InstanceId)\t\(.VpcId)\t\(.InstanceType)"' || echo "No instances or error" done
